root_motivation: Today identity is a carried credential: a client must call signup, redeem a key, and pass it as a header or tenant_key argument on every call -- a flow the PM rejected twice in two days as too complicated. Every tenant gets a secret personal URL (https://mcphost.dev/u/<secret>/mcp) that is its whole credential instead: pasting the URL into a client is the entire onboarding, the URL is as rotatable as the key already is, and a human can mint one from a web page in one click.
user_persona: A person with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, claude.ai, or Cursor who wants an agent on mcphost with no signup/redeem/key dance; an agent on a URL-bound session that needs to tell its human what its own URL is; a tenant whose URL leaked and needs it dead in one call.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant with a URL secret, When a streamable-HTTP tools/call host.whoami is POSTed to /u/<secret>/mcp with no Authorization header and no tenant_key, Then the result names that tenant with auth_method: "url".
Given a random or rotated secret, When any request hits /u/<wrong>/mcp, Then HTTP 404 with the standard error body, no WWW-Authenticate header, and no resource-metadata link.
Given a URL-bound session, When host.key_rotate is called, Then the response carries a new key and a new URL, the old URL returns 404 on the next request, and the old key is tenant_key_invalid.

Given a browser, When GET /u/new then the button's POST /u/new run, Then a tenant exists with source: "url-page", the page shows the URL and four copy snippets, and a sixth POST from the same IP within the hour is refused with the signup limiter's error.
Given GET /u/<secret>/mcp with a browser Accept: text/html, When fetched, Then a short text page explains the URL and how to add it, and the response is not an MCP error.
Given a URL-bound session, When host.quickstart kind=echo is called, Then the response has no signup step and authenticated: true.
Given a request on /u/<secret>/mcp carrying an Authorization: Bearer for a different tenant, When dispatched, Then the error class is auth_conflict and no call is executed.

Given the landed binary deployed on prod and a fresh URL minted at https://mcphost.dev/u/new, When that URL is added to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, claude.ai, and Cursor and each runs host.whoami, Then all four return the same tenant with auth_method: "url" and none shows an OAuth or login prompt.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a secret URL need to exist when the tenant_key argument already works on any client that can set a header or pass an argument?
five_whys_trace.a: Several real MCP clients (Claude Desktop custom connectors, claude.ai, Cursor's mcp.json) have no UI for a bearer header or a tool-call argument -- their only input is a URL.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just put the tenant_key in the URL's query string instead of a whole new path/secret scheme?
five_whys_trace.a: A query string is logged by proxies and browser history by default in a way a path segment that this host explicitly redacts is not, and a path-based secret reuses the exact precedent this codebase already has (/hook/{id}).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the path secret have to outrank the Authorization header in the Auth precedence chain instead of slotting in after it?
five_whys_trace.a: A /u/<secret>/mcp URL is meant to be the WHOLE credential with nothing else required -- if the header won by default, a stale or wrong header on the same connection would silently shadow the URL's own tenant, defeating 'paste the URL and nothing else.'

five_whys_trace.q: Why refuse outright (auth_conflict) rather than just trusting the path secret whenever both are present?
five_whys_trace.a: Silently picking one of two valid-but-different credentials is exactly the kind of ambiguous resolution this codebase's own ConflictingCredentials/WrongTenant precedents already refuse, so a caller never discovers after the fact which tenant it actually ran as.

five_whys_trace.q: Why 404 instead of 401 for a wrong/rotated secret?
five_whys_trace.a: A 401 (or any response shaped differently for 'wrong' vs 'doesn't exist') would let a prober distinguish a once-valid rotated secret from a pure guess; 404 byte-identical to an unmapped route leaks nothing.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should every tenant get a URL secret eagerly at signup (requirement 2's literal 'generated at tenant creation for every new tenant'), or only lazily when first needed?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Implemented lazily only, via host.key_rotate (always rotates/mints) and the /u/new page's own first-time mint -- no AC in this dispatch's assigned list tests eager generation at every signup, and signup's own JSON response field set is pinned byte-for-byte by tests/handoff_ac05_raw_signup_still_works_unchanged.rs, which a new field would break.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should host.whoami disclose the plaintext URL for a key-authenticated (non-URL-bound) session, per requirement 3's 'or just-created session' clause?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Out of scope for this dispatch's AC list (none of AC1-7 test host.whoami's own url/url_set fields) -- host.whoami's auth_method now reports "url" when resolved via the path secret (AC1), but no plaintext-disclosure logic beyond that was added, since the plaintext is only ever available at the moment of generation/rotation (host.key_rotate's own response, or the /u/new page) and is never recoverable from the stored hash afterward.
